articleTitle: Analysis and Parameter Design for Voltage-Controlled VSCs Using Sigma-Delta Current Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: This paper tries to apply Sigma-Delta ADCs to inverter current sampling for active damping in voltage-controlled VSCs. The model of SD-ADCs is given and aliasing of current sampling with SD-ADCs is analyzed. An anti-aliasing synchronization method for average current sampling with SD-ADCs is proposed. Phase lag in the feedback loop caused by sinc filter is analyzed and optimal active damping coefficient is determined. Finally, simulation and experimental results validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Natural Cooling Half-Bridge GaN Module in CCM Boost Converter with Low Parasitic Impedance and High Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: A high-density natural cooling half-bridge power module for a top-cooled 650-V GaN HEMTs is proposed in this paper. Compared with Si and SiC devices, GaN HEMTs has advantages, such as low on-resistance, low drive loss, low switching loss and small size. However, it also have challenges such as large switching oscillations and small heat dissipation area. This paper proposes a PCB layout scheme with low parasitic impedance and bipolar gate drive with +6V/-3V. It keeps GaN devices completely on one side of the PCB while makes the parasitic inductance of the power loop within 1nH. Hence, the installation of heat sinks becomes easier. This paper verifies the above design in a CCM boost converter that widely used in photovoltaic and energy storage systems. A loss evaluation based the spice model of GaN device GS66516T is given. Finally, a 2.5kW experimental prototype with the proposed power module is manufactured. It was tested to get peak efficiency of 99.14% and full-load efficiency of 99.09%. The experimental results show that the temperature rise of GaN HEMTs is limited within 50°C in a windless environment, which effectively proves the rationality of the proposed power module design and loss evaluation method.

articleTitle: A Black-Box Modeling Method Based on LSTM Network for DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Modeling power electronic converters is of great importance for verifying the stability and power quality of the power systems containing multiple power electronics devices. However, due to complicated inner structures, protected intellectual property, or other reasons, fidelity of system-level modeling and simulation is difficult to be ensured. A data-driven black-box modeling method for DC-DC converters powering pulsated power loads is presented based on the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. The complicated operation conditions of the input voltage and load current of converters are analyzed and firstly targeted for modeling. Then, the structure and hyper-parameters of the presented model is designed. Finally, the dataset for training, validation and test is obtained by sampling the voltages and currents of the target converter and then used for modeling. The fidelity of the DC-DC converter's model under more general operation conditions can be improved by the presented black-box model. The feasibility and accuracy of the presented method is verified by dataset acquired in experiments.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Battery System Temperature Field Based on Three-Dimensional Thermal Equivalent Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are extensively utilized across various fields, but their thermal fragility has been seriously concerned. Lithium-ion batteries are easily affected by working temperature, therefore, monitoring the internal temperature of batteries is crucial. In addition, under the action of various composite factors, the temperature inside the battery system usually appears uneven during charging and discharging, which leads to the acceleration of battery aging and the intensification of battery inconsistency. Therefore, reconstructing the temperature field of the battery system can provide multidimensional thermal information that is beneficial to temperature prediction and significantly improve the effectiveness of thermal management of the battery system. Compared with single battery, the temperature estimation of battery system becomes more difficult due to the increase of size and the complex interaction of multiple heat sources. A three-dimensional distributed thermal equivalent circuit modeling method for battery system is proposed, and its model accuracy is validated through experiments. This method offers high accuracy, is adaptable to different battery types, allows for rapid calculation of temperature values at all designated points within the battery system, and enables real-time reconstruction of the temperature field distribution.

articleTitle: An Improved Digital Power Measurement Algorithm with Window Functions for Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The real-time digital measurement technique is one of the most important issues for the smart power substation. To enhance the ability of substations to measure electric power and to address the challenges of substation metering data not being able to be centrally computed and the difficulty of handling massive multi-time frequency data computation at the power substation. A new digital power measurement method is proposed based on the Hanning window function to reduce the spectral leakage. The signal is converted from the time domain to the frequency domain using a fully-phase fast Fourier transform, and harmonic parameters are obtained through polynomial approximation-based single-spectrum interpolation. The calculation accuracy is enhanced by using a variable forgetting factor Recursive Least Squares algorithm, with coefficients updated through an adaptive linear combiner, significantly improving the speed and accuracy of the measurement for power substation.

articleTitle: Inductance Characteristics Elimination Method Embedding in Grid-Following Inverter with Consideration of Regulated Capacity Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: For the low voltage distribution area with regulated capacity transformer, the variation of transformer capacity will lead to the grid-side impedance change. This dynamic scenario increases the risk of harmonic resonance occurrence. Impedance model of low voltage distribution area with regulated capacity transformer and grid-connected inverter are built to analyze the system stability under different transformer capacities. Then, considering the various inductance characteristics of regulated capacity transformer, an inductance characteristics elimination method is proposed by inducing virtual negative inductance. Finally, simulations verify the correctness of the above analysis.

articleTitle: Stability Boundary Characterization and Inner Loop Controller Design for Grid Forming Converters Based on D-Partition Method
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The expanding incorporation of renewable energy sources has led to a notable rise in the application of grid forming (GFM) converters within power systems. However, in weak grid conditions, poor design of inner loop parameters can lead to severe stability problems in GFM converters. This paper presents inner loop controller design for GFM converters based on D-partition method, providing stability boundary characterization for control parameters that meet multiple performance criteria such as phase margin, gain margin, and short-circuit ratio. This method allows for the quick and accurate determination of inner loop control parameters through graphical visualization, thus eliminating the need for repetitive trial-and-error adjustments. The proposed design method's effectiveness is demonstrated on a 25kW experimental platform.

articleTitle: Conditions for ZVS of Buck Converters Considering Nonidealities
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) is widely used to increase the efficiency of converters. It is influenced by some nonidealities, including the MOSFET's junction capacitance and the dead-time. The buck converters may lose the ZVS operation when the junction capacitance incompletely charges or discharges during the dead-time. This paper aims to discuss the influence of nonlinear junction capacitance and dead-time on the ZVS region of buck converters and propose a method to get the boundary condition of ZVS, considering the interaction of these nonidealities. A 600V buck converter based on SiC MOSFET is built. The experimental results prove the correctness of the ZVS critical conditions with inductance and dead-time.

articleTitle: An Improved AC-Precharging Strategy for the Startup Process of Modular Multilevel Converters Based on Time-Domain Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The modular multilevel converter (MMC) has emerged as the most attractive conversion technology for high-voltage dc (HVDC) transmission systems. The startup process of MMC is essential for normal operation. The startup process of HBSM-MMC and FBSM-MMC is analyzed in this paper. Due to the different conduction paths, the capacitor voltage of HBSM and FBSM are different in the uncontrolled precharging stage. Then, it is explained that the reference voltage of FBSM cannot be tracked during controlled AC stratup process. Furthermore, an improved AC-precharging strategy for FBSM-MMC is proposed, which DC-component and AC-component are controlled separately. Finally, the simulation and experiment are performed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed pre-charging strategy.

articleTitle: Analytical Model of Core Energy Capacitance of Gapped Magnetic Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The high-frequency operating characteristics of inductors are determined by their stray capacitance, which can lead to current ringing and electromagnetic interference. The research on the stray capacitance of inductor windings is relatively mature, however, there is limited research on the capacitance related to magnetic cores. The electric field intensity in the air gaps of magnetic cores can be relatively high, making the energy capacitance nonnegligible. Therefore, this paper proposes an approximate calculation method for the boundary potential of distributed air gaps in rod NiZn magnetic cores. The model is verified using finite element analysis (FEA), providing a reference for the design of gapped inductors.

articleTitle: Bidirectional DC-DC Converter With Zero Current Ripple and Low Voltage Stress for Power Battery Equalization Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Active equalizer is a significant approach to break through the inconsistent charging of power batteries, which can improve the available capacity, endurance mileage and system safety of the electric vehicles. As the important part of active equalizer, a bidirectional converter which possesses zero current ripple on the high voltage side (HVS) and small current ripple on the low voltage side (LVS), low voltage stress with wider conversion ratio, common ground and positive polarity between the LVS and HVS, is proposed in this paper. Therefore, with the proposed converter, the improved efficiency, speed and reliability of the active equalizer can be realized. The operating principles of the converter in boost mode to achieve cell-to-string (C2S) equalization and in buck mode to complete string-to-cell (S2C) equalization are analyzed. Besides, the detailed mathematical model and related simulations are presented to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed converter in the equalization system.

articleTitle: Design of Partially High-Temperature Superconducting Planar Motor for Semiconductor Optical Lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Superconducting motors should further be improved in their performance to realize high-performance optical lithographic machines to meet the huge and growing demands for manufacturing integrated circuits (ICs) in the semiconductor industry. In this paper, a moving-coil coreless partially high-temperature superconducting (HTS) planar motor is proposed to satisfy such demands. The proposed motor has both the stator and the mover inside a cryostat, which are cooled by a single-stage GM cryocooler and a radiation heat transfer respectively, and the stator has direct current HTS coils made of rare-earth barium-copper-oxide (ReBCO) instead of permanent magnets. The design process of the proposed motor described involves the calculation of motor force, stator flux density, HTS coil current, HTS temperature, alternating current losses of superconductor, and a heat loss of cryostat. The designed motor is compared with the conventional motor, and the comparison shows that the proposed motor is superior to the conventional motor in terms of stage acceleration at the same superconductor temperatures from 20K to 40K, mover ohmic loss, and simple cooling of mover coils.

articleTitle: A Novel LLC Converter with Split Transformers for Output Current Ripple Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: A novel LLC converter with split transformers (STs) which can suppress the output current ripple is proposed. By utilizing non-equal-turns-ratios (NET) in two series-connected transformers, distinct magnetizing currents are generated, and then, achieving the suppression of output current ripple which is a significant issue with the conventional LLC converters. The output capacitors can thus be reduced for achieving high power density and it is possible to achieve electrolytic-capacitor-less for improving the system lifespan and reliability. Furthermore, the proposed NET-ST LLC converter also promises high efficiency with zero-voltage switching (ZVS) for the primary-side switches across the entire operating range and zero-current switching (ZCS) for a portion of the secondary-side rectifier diodes.

articleTitle: Electrical Power System Adaptive Design for Powered-Down Launch Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Batch production and multi-satellite launches are critical techniques in the construction of internet satellite constellations. They require simplification of the interface between satellites and launch vehicles for the sake of cost control and operation process optimization in launch sites. Learning from successful practice in the field of micro-satellite development, powered-down launch technology is certain to be applied in low orbit internet constellation satellites. Compared with powered-on launch utilized in traditional large communication satellites, powered-down launch requires new analysis in satellites' power system design. This paper discussed the relevant topics.

articleTitle: The Triple Phase-Shift Control of DAB Converter with Reconfigurable Transformer to Optimize the RMS Current for Wide Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: This work proposes a triple phase-shift (TPS) control for a dual active bridge (DAB) DC-DC converter with reconfigurable transformer (RTDAB) to improve its efficiency over a wide voltage range. By optimizing the inductor rms current of the RTDAB under TPS control in different working modes, the proposed control method can achieve a lower rms current under a wide voltage range. The proposed control method is obtained on the basis of the traditional TPS control of DAB converter and does not require complicated mathematical processing. The control approach is easy to implement. Finally, simulation results on the MATLAB/Simulink platform demonstrate the efficiency of the suggested strategy.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Strategy for Hydrogen-Containing Hybrid Energy Storage Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The study introduces the Dynamic Response Regulation System, which considers the multi-state of hydrogen energy. This novel approach addresses the power discrepancy resulting from response delays in electrolyzers and fuel cells. The system integrates batteries and supercapacitors to form a response compensation mechanism, which proposes a power distribution strategy that considers the supercapacitor's state of charge (SOC). The system demonstrates proficiency in the management of power fluctuations across a range of frequencies, thereby ensuring the stability of the microgrid's operation. A hydrogen storage energy management strategy has been formulated based on the actual response of the battery and the state of charge (SOC), with the objective of further enhancing the system's efficiency in maintaining power balance and the stability of the direct current bus voltage. The case analysis and simulation results substantiate the efficacy of this innovative system in attaining the aforementioned objectives.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Modulation Strategy for Single-Stage Semi-Bridge Matrix AC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The single-stage half-bridge matrix (SBM) converter has attracted considerable attention owing to its high power density and efficiency. However, substantial variations in input AC voltage and the influence of bridge arm capacitors on inductor current fluctuations pose challenges for existing modulation strategies to ensure efficient operation across the entire operating range. Therefore, this paper proposes a high-efficiency, multi-degree-of-freedom (DOF) modulation strategy for the SBM converter. This strategy minimizes the root mean square current and guarantees zero-voltage switching for all power switches, thereby optimizing the converter's efficiency over a broad input voltage range while taking into consideration the impact of bridge arm capacitors. Firstly, a time-domain analysis of the three-DOF modulation strategy is conducted. Subsequently, optimization is achieved by reducing the peak-to-peak current, and its steady-state characteristics are compared with those of recent related studies. Finally, an experimental prototype is constructed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed modulation strategy. The results indicate that the proposed strategy can improve efficiency by approximately 6.61% compared to recent optimization approaches.

articleTitle: Constant Frequency Modulation Strategy for DAB-LLC Sigma Converter to Achieve Voltage Regulation with Wide ZVS Range
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The bidirectional converter based on DAB-LLC Sigma structure, merging the high efficiency of LLC with the superior controllability of DAB, has attracted intensive research attention in recent years. In order to accomplish voltage regulation and soft switching in a wide range, two constant frequency modulation strategies based on different sub-converters regulating voltage are presented in this paper. For the control strategy of DAB voltage regulation, a hybrid modulation strategy is studied in this paper, which can realize soft switching in a full load range. For the control strategy of LLC voltage regulation, a centrally symmetric PWM control is applied to LLC to regulate voltage and DAB operates at single phase shift (SPS) modulation to implement auxiliary power regulation. And the feasibility of these strategies is confirmed through results.

articleTitle: Study on Transient Stability of Grid-Forming Inverters During Islanded to Grid Connected Mode Transition Embedded with Priority Current Limiter
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Conventional transient stability analysis for grid forming inverter from islanded to grid connected mode paid high attention on the nonlinear behavior under different grid strength and different control parameters. However, the grid forming inverter with voltage source nature suffers from the overcurrent risk under large power angle deviation, but the impact of current limiter is overlooked in previous study. Moreover, the nonlinear behavior is overlooked with unknown load. In this paper, the transient stability analysis for grid forming inverter transitioning from islanded to grid connected mode is carried out. It shows that when the resistive-capacitive load that satisfies certain condition will enable the inverter shows totally inverted transient instability or undesired stable operation under current saturation mode risk under same power angle response direction. The findings in this paper provided a physical insight into the nonlinear process of the mode transition and shed light on transient stability improvement design. The findings are verified based on a 500W experimental platform.

articleTitle: Grid-Forming Photovoltaic-Energy Storage System with Higher Flexibility Based on DC-Link Voltage Synchronization Control
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: As the grid strength gradually weakens, there is an urgent need to enhance the weak grid adaptability and precise control capability of photovoltaic-energy storage (PV-ES) systems. This paper analyzes the basic principles of the PV-ES virtual synchronous generator (PV-ES VSG) control scheme under the common DC bus. A flexible control scheme for grid-connected PV-ES systems is proposed based on DC-link voltage synchronization control (DVSC). Compared to existing PV-ES VSG control schemes, the proposed scheme can significantly improve the control flexibility of the energy storage and increase the diversity of its control algorithms, while maintaining similar power support capabilities and grid-connected performance. This improvement not only optimizes the performance of the energy storage unit in the power grid, but also reduces its burden and pressure on DC bus voltage control. Simulation results based on MATLAB/Simulink and the experiment results based on the Hardware-In-Loop (HIL) platform validate the effectiveness and rationality of the proposed scheme. The comparison with the PV-ES VSG also shows the advantages of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Assessment of Safe Operating Regions and Methods for Enhancing Static Capacity in Hybrid Three-Level Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The continuous development and utilization of new energy sources have underscored the increasing prominence of Voltage Source Converters (VSCs), emphasizing the need for efficient and cost-effective power conversion systems. The hybrid three-level topology, which optimally balances cost and efficiency, presents significant potential for future applications. However, the loss and junction temperature characteristics of hybrid three-level topologies remain inadequately understood. This paper introduces a novel loss analysis and junction temperature calculation method to determine the four-quadrant operating capabilities and output capacities at various voltage levels for hybrid three-level topologies. Furthermore, by analyzing the loss and junction temperature distribution patterns, an optimal capacity configuration method is proposed. To enhance performance further, a device capacity optimization configuration method tailored for hybrid three-level topologies is developed. Comprehensive simulations validate that the hybrid three-level topology achieves high efficiency at lower costs compared to the full SiC topology, while also offering the added benefit of static capacity expansion.

articleTitle: Improved Single-Stage DC-DC-AC Three Active Bridge Converter Based on Port Energy Decoupling
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The load used in electroacoustic transmitter systems exhibits short-term pulse characteristics. High peak-to-average power ratio is a challenge for peak power and reliability of power supplies. This paper proposes an improved single-stage DC-DC-AC triple active bridge converter. Smoothing the power supply pulsation power through integrated energy storage port. By adding a hardware decoupling network, the energy decoupling among the energy storage port and the load port can be realized, reduces the impact of energy fluctuations at the storage port on the load port and ensures a stable AC output.

articleTitle: Hybrid Interleaving Control Strategy for Interleaved Flyback Microinverter
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The flyback converter is widely adopted due to its simple structure and compact form factor. An interleaved flyback converter can further enhance power capability. To increase energy transmission density, the system typically operates in Boundary Conduction Mode (BCM). However, this mode often leads to incomplete interleaving of the primary transformer current near power peaks due to an excessive duty cycle. To address this issue, this study introduces a control method that incorporates a constant primary peak current in a variable frequency discontinuous conduction mode (VF-DCM). This strategy can limit the maximum duty cycle by setting a constant value for the primary peak current, thereby ensuring complete interleaving of the total input and output currents near the power peaks. Considering the high voltages and currents that the switching devices endure near the power peaks, a resonant period compensation is adopted to enable zero-voltage switching (ZVS). The proposed method is substantiated through detailed simulations conducted using PLECS software, which confirm that the approach can achieve complete interleaving across the entire operational range, reduce the ripple in total input and output currents and lower the harmonic content in the grid current.

articleTitle: The Overview of Frequency Regulation Coordinated Control for MMC-HVDC Connecting Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Modular multilevel converter based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) transmission is the mainstream technology for offshore wind farms with long distances of more than 80km integration. With the development of technology, the frequency stability problem due to the low inertia has become the focus of the current research. This paper systematically discusses the coordinated frequency regulation control strategy of MMC-HVDC with wind farms. The common symmetrical monopole/ bipolar MMC-HVDC system structures in engineering are first introduced. Next, The frequency regulation control for MMC-HVDC and wind farms (WFs) and the frequency sensing method used for coordination are summarized. Finally, this paper looks forward to the future research direction of MMC-HVDC connecting wind farms regarding frequency regulation capability assessment, and grid-forming fault ride-through control.

articleTitle: An Integrated Charger of Wireless Power Transfer, Onboard Charger, and Auxiliary Power Module for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Battery is a key component of Electric Vehicles (EVs), which has sparked a great demand for improvement in the EVs charging system. This paper proposes an integrated charging system for wireless power transfer (WPT), Onboard charger (OBC), and auxiliary power module (APM). The receiving coil on the secondary side can be weakly coupled with the transmitting coil of WPT and strongly coupled with the transmitting coil of OBC. Using a transformer on the receiving side to integrate the APM into the circuit. In this way, receiving coil, compensation network, and power electronics converter can be shared. The integrated structure can work in three working patterns. In the WPT mode and OBC mode, power grid delivers energy to the EV batteries, high-voltage (HV) batteries and low-voltage (LV) batteries can be charged at the same time. In the APM mode, HV batteries power LV batteries. In the traditional EV charger, WPT, OBC, and APM are three separate systems. This paper integrates three charging systems with the advantages of high-power density and cost effectiveness. The experimental results verify the proposal.

articleTitle: A High-Power Converter for Electrolytic Hydrogen Production Based on DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: In the wind-solar-hydrogen storage DC microgrid architecture, the hydrogen production link needs to use a DC-DC converter to connect the DC bus and the electrolyzer. According to the characteristics of alkaline electrolyzer and DC microgrids, a two-stage DC/DC converter as the supply of the electrolyzer is proposed in this paper. Specifically, the front stage of the cascade converter is composed of two multi-resonant modules, which adopt the structure of input series and output parallel to adapt to the DC bus of higher voltage levels. The rear stage of the cascade converter adopts three-phase interleaved Buck to reduce the influence of load sudden change on the front stage. This two-stage converter is able to meet the requirements of high-voltage input as well as low-voltage and high-current output, and has the characteristics of high step-down ratio, high efficiency and electrical isolation. In addition, considering that the actual resonance parameters may be different, the power imbalance between the two modules in the front stage is analyzed, and a control method suitable for the cascade converter is designed, and its effectiveness is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: A Fully-Interleaved Stacked-Half-Bridge Single-Stage 48V-1V Voltage Regulator
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: In the architecture of point-of-load power supply in data center power system, 48V bus is gradually replacing 12V bus due to its lower conduction loss, and the 48V-1V single-stage high current high step-down converter has become a promising candidate for the third power stage. This paper compares the characteristics of single-stage multi-phase parallel and multi-element stacked structures in improving voltage step-down ratio and current carrying capacity. A fully interleaved stacked-half-bridge structure is proposed. The influence of the number of stacked elements on converter characteristics is discussed, and the optimal parameter configuration is found. Compared with the conventional solution, the proposed structure achieves a lower transformer turn ratio. Planar magnetic components are employed to reduce the height of the prototype, and a planar coupled inductor with five-leg core is proposed to achieve coupling of all output inductors. A 48V-1V/100A prototype was built, operating at 300kHz with a peak efficiency of 86.2%.

articleTitle: Hybrid DCM/CCM Modulation Strategy for Dual-Active-Bridge Microinverter
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: In response to the increasing demands for high efficiency, convenience, and low cost in micro-photovoltaic grid-connected inverters, this paper investigates a dual active bridge (DAB) microinverter. This microinverter is designed to achieve high power density in the conversion of electrical energy while facilitating soft switching across a wide range of grid voltages. The operation of the inverter can be categorized into discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) and continuous conduction mode (CCM), depending on the characteristics of the transformer leakage current. This paper introduces a hybrid modulation strategy that alternates between DCM and CCM by designing the trajectory of the primary-side switch drive duty cycle throughout the operating frequency cycle. This modulation strategy ensures that all switches operate with zero-voltage switching (ZVS) or zero-current switching (ZCS) under both heavy and light load conditions. Simulation results are provided to validate the proposed model and control strategy.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage rTMS Pulse Generation Circuit with High-Current and Low-Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: This article proposes a two-stage power converter with novel control methods for repeated Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS). The first stage is a Series Resonant Converter (SRC), which changes the average current of its output by changing the switching frequency and is supplemented by a larger intermediate capacitor to achieve average power transmission, decrease the front-stage converter design capacity, and reduce the pulse impact of the input side. The second level is the pulse generation circuit of the multiplexing rTMS pulse generation circuit switch, which not only plays the role of pulse generation but also transmits the capacitor energy of the intermediate capacitor to the backward pulse generation circuit to compensate the loss of the circuit during operation, at the same time, using a dual coil coupling simulation scheme can effectively avoid the problem of parallel current sharing of multiple devices in high current situations. The circuit is controlled by the output capacitance voltage to ensure the stimulation intensity (current intensity) of the output pulse. Finally, an experimental prototype with a pulse magnetic stimulation frequency of 25Hz and pulse current peak value of 2000A was set up in the laboratory. The results showed the feasibility of the proposed circuit topology and control method. Finally, an experimental prototype with a pulse magnetic stimulation frequency of 25Hz and pulse current peak value of 1000A was set up in the laboratory. The results showed the feasibility of the proposed circuit topology and control method.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Breakdown Characteristics and Insulation Failure Analysis of Epoxy Resin for Power Electronic Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Insulation systems in power electronic transformers are subjected to long-term high-frequency and high-voltage electrical stress, increasing the risk of failure. This study prepared epoxy resin samples for encapsulation insulation in power electronic transformers and tested their high-frequency breakdown characteristics in the 10 kHz to 100 kHz range, analyzing the results using Weibull distribution. Scanning electron microscopy was utilized to investigate the microstructure of the epoxy resin after high-frequency insulation failure. The results showed that the high-frequency breakdown strength conformed to the Weibull distribution, with the scale parameter decreasing and gradually reaching a threshold as frequency increased, ranging from approximately 66 kV/mm to 84 kV/mm. The epoxy resin samples prepared using the scraping method exhibited no significant insulation defects in their morphology. Post-insulation failure, the surface and cross-sectional morphology of the epoxy resin displayed distinct characteristic features.

articleTitle: Insulation Optimization of PCB Busbar for an ANPC Converter Using 15 kV SiC Module
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: In 10kV medium-voltage distribution networks, higher electric field strengths demand more stringent insulation. Merely increasing the insulation layer thickness of busbar can lead to excessive parasitic inductance, degraded switching performance, significant switching losses and electromagnetic interference, particularly in high-frequency applications. This paper utilizes finite element simulation to optimize insulation for an ANPC converter using 15kV SiC MOSFETs and proposes a partial discharge (PD) free optimization strategy. The thickness of the final PCB busbar is only 6.09 mm, and partial discharge test as well as insulation resistance tests are conducted at +8 kV/-8 kV voltage. The results show that this design exhibits symmetrical parasitic parameters, low commutation loop inductance, and high insulation capability. The optimized design ensures efficient and reliable operation of high-voltage converters, meeting the stringent requirements for modern power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Research on Wireless Power and Information Transmission Technology for Underwater Renewable Energy Source
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer(WPT)effectively solves the problems of corrosion and leakage in underwater environments using the traditional plug-and-play charging method. In this paper, an underwater simultaneous wireless power and information transmission system based on magnetic induction coupling is investigated. Based on the combination of double-sided LCC compensation topology and wave-blocking network, four basic topologies of signal transmission are modeled, and then the signal transmission voltage gain and the influence of the energy channel on the signal channel under the four topologies are analyzed. Furthermore, the advantages and disadvantages of the simulation effects of the four topologies are compared, so as to validate the feasibility and correctness of the performance of the simultaneous wireless power and information transmission system and realize full-duplex signals transmission.

Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless power and information transmission

articleTitle: A Frequency Adaptive Selection of Multi-Frequency Impedance Measurement Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: As more and more power electronic equipments are incorporated into the grid, the new power system is becoming increasingly unstable. This is usually due to the impedance mismatch between different power electronic converters. Therefore, accurate impedance measurement technology plays an important role in ensuring the stability of power system. Multi-sinusoidal signal has become a common impedance measurement method because of its accuracy and rapidity. The traditional multi-sinusoidal signal is selected by equidistant multiple sinusoidal signals. In the absence of guiding theory, the selection of frequency interval always relies on experience accumulation, resulting in low accuracy, low reliability and large manual intervention. In order to solve the above problems, a Dynamic Mean Thresholding (DMT) method for adaptive frequency selection of multiple sinusoidal signals is proposed. The DMT method calculates the average error of all impedance measurement points, and then selects the points with greater than the average error for the next iteration. Compared with traditional methods, DMT method has higher measurement accuracy and less manual intervention. Finally, the proposed impedance measurement scheme is verified by HIL experiment platform

articleTitle: Steady-State Modeling of a Matrix-Type AC-DC DAB Converter Considering AC-Side Capacitor Voltage Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The matrix-type dual-active-bridge (DAB) converter is attractive for single-stage ac-dc power conversion, known for its high efficiency and reliability. Unlike conventional dc-dc DAB converters, which typically feature large dc-side filter capacitance to maintain constant dc voltage throughout each switching cycle, the matrix-type ac-dc converter employs small ac-side capacitance. This design achieves a high power factor and optimize both power density and cost. However, the small ac-side capacitance results in noticeable capacitor voltage ripple during the switching cycle, which cannot be ignored. This paper develops a time-domain steady-state model to accurately characterize the steady-state performance of the converter. It is revealed for the first time that the ac-side capacitor voltage ripple can substantially impact the performance of the converter, particularly by potentially compromising zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) operation, thereby reducing power conversion efficiency and worsening electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues. Both simulation and experimental results validate the theoretical analysis and the findings.

articleTitle: Turn-Off Voltage Overshoot Sensing for SiC MOSFETs Based on Electroluminescence Spectra Detection and Support Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Sensing the turn-off voltage overshoot in silicon carbide (SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) is critically important for enhancing the reliability of converters. However, existing peak sampling measurement schemes face numerous challenges, such as high static errors and slow dynamic response. Given the correlation between the electroluminescence spectral characteristics and device operation states, this work proposes a method for sensing turn-off voltage overshoots based on spectral detection results and support vector regression (SVR), with an average sensing error of 5.01V.

articleTitle: Topology of H5-D Non-Isolated PV Grid-Connected Inverter Based on Active Power Decoupling
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: With the development of distributed photovoltaic industry, household photovoltaic and energy storage equipment has gradually become a research hotspot. The non-isolated inverter topology can cater well to the characteristics of miniaturization and compactness of household inverters. However, non-isolated inverters have problems of electromagnetic compatibility and stability due to common mode current in parasitic capacitors. Otherwise, power fluctuations of twice the fundamental frequency on the AC side will be coupled to the DC side. This paper presents a non-isolated inverter with common mode current suppression and active power decoupling.

articleTitle: TGT: Battery State of Charge Estimation with Robustness to Missing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: In recent years, with the large-scale application of new energy sources, whole-life battery state-of-condition (SOC) estimation has become increasingly important in power systems and electric vehicle range. However, existing SOC estimation methods such as ARIMA and machine learning methods such as Transformer have insufficient accuracy to solve estimation problems in long-term sequences. Based on this, this paper proposes a novel TCN-GRU-Transformer (TGT) model that aims to optimize the performance of SOC estimation in scenarios with different degrees of missing data. The model captures the global dependencies in the battery data by extracting useful features from the time-series dataset to understand the trend of the battery state over time. Through experiments on publicly available datasets, it is demonstrated that the MAE of the TGT model is 0.0192 while classical machine learning models is 0.030 in battery soc estimation. The error rate decreases by 36.1% in MAE.

articleTitle: Research on Orderly Charging Strategy for Electric Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic and PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The disorderly charging of electric vehicles (EVs) increases the peak valley difference of load and users' charging costs, and the traditional orderly charging strategy requires users to input information manually. This article proposes an orderly charging strategy for electric vehicles based on fuzzy logic and particle swarm optimization algorithm. By comprehensively considering the initial SOC and daily average driving mileage of electric vehicles, a fuzzy logic model is used to determine whether the EV participates in orderly charging optimization, without the need for vehicle owners to input information. Aiming to minimize the peak valley difference of the load curve and the total charging cost of the user, the charging plan is optimized through particle swarm optimization algorithm. Compared with the disorderly charging calculated by Monte Carlo algorithm, the case analysis shows that the proposed strategy can effectively reduce the peak valley difference and users' charging costs.

articleTitle: Optimized Modulation Strategy for DAB-Type Three-Phase Single-Stage Isolated AC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: For a dual-active-bridge type three-phase single-stage isolated AC-DC converter topology, to suppress DC bias of transformer current, the conventional modulation strategy regulates transformer current by limiting the three-phase shift angles but leads to a restriction of system transfer power. In this paper, a new modulation strategy for a dual-active-bridge type three-phase single-stage isolated AC-DC converter topology is proposed. By introducing a new initial phase-shift angle, the modulation can decouple adjacent switching cycle transformer current without limiting the range of the conventional three phase-shift angles so that the power transfer capacity of the system is unrestricted. In addition, the system power transfer characteristic of proposed modulation strategy is also analyzed in this paper. The effectiveness of proposed modulation is validated by simulation.

articleTitle: PCC dq-Frame Based Power Loop Modeling and Stability Analysis of Grid-Following Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: For large-scale renewable energy power generation plants, the impedance model based stability analysis method, which describes the dynamic characteristics between instantaneous voltage and current of the converter terminal, has the advantages of clear physical meaning and simple model for system stability analysis. However, the impedance model generally takes the converter terminal as the modeling benchmark, which requires coordinate conversion due to the feeder dynamics and thus is difficult to realize unified modeling in complex systems. Besides, people in power system community pay more attention to the dynamics of power rather than voltage and current. Therefore, in this paper, a power loop model of grid-following (GFL) converters based on the PCC dq-frame is proposed, which can simple the modeling and analysis of the large-scale renewable energy power generation plants. Furthermore, the Nyquist criterion are adopted to analysis the self-stability of GFL converters by the proposed power loop model. Simulation and experimental results are finally provided to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed model and the stability analysis.

articleTitle: A Partial Power Converter Based on Hybrid Control L-LLC
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: This proposes an L-LLC converter with partial power processing.By employing a hybrid control strategy that combines primary-side phase-shifting with frequency modulation, the L-LLC resonant converter reduces the variation in switching frequency, resulting in improved overall efficiency. The working principle and operational characteristics of the partial power processing L-LLC converter based on this hybrid control method is analyzed in detail. A 4kW prototype was used to verify the correctness and reliability of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Active Capacitor-Based Transient Power Suppression for Electromechanical Collaborative Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Airborne and ship-borne power systems are stand-alone power systems composed of generators and various power electronic converters. The response speed of the generator is much lower than that of the power electronic converter. The rapid load power transient will lead to significant fluctuation of the DC bus voltage, and also may threaten the safe and stable operation of the generator. This paper studies the transient power active suppression method based on the active capacitor converter. Firstly, the active rectifier is used to match the response speed of the generator by limiting the rate of change of the rectifier input power. Then, the disturbance of the load power to the generator is avoided. And an active capacitor converter is used to compensate the instantaneous deviation of the output power and the load power of the rectifier, thereby ensuring the fast response speed of the power system when the load fluctuates rapidly, while avoiding fluctuations in the bus voltage. The architecture and operation principle of the transient load power suppression based on active capacitors are presented, the corresponding control strategy is studied, and the energy management method of energy storage capacitors is analyzed as well. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the presented method is verified with experimental results.

articleTitle: Research on a Novel Soft-Switching Buck Converter Based on Energy Feedforward
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: In the traditional ZVT soft-switching DC-DC converters, the resonant energy transmission path is complicated and the auxiliary switches may operate in hard switching. This paper proposes an energy-feedforward ZVT soft-switching Buck converter, all the switches keep soft-switching operation, and the resonant energy is transmitted directly to the load through the forward transformer instead of returning to the source or indirectly flowing to load, which is conducive to improve the conversion efficiency. After theoretical analysis, the design process of key parameters is given, and verified through simulation. Finally, an experimental prototype is constructed with 200W output, 200kHz operating frequency. The experimental results show that soft-switching operation of all switches is maintained in load range from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to rated power. Compared with the traditional hard-switching Buck, the voltage and current spike of the main switch are reduced largely, the efficiency is better in the whole test range, improved from 94.54% to 97.34% at full load.

articleTitle: Hydrogen Production from Directly Electrolyzing Seawater
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The principal endeavors include three impacts. Development of a pulsed hydrogen production circuit model, accompanied by the design of power control loops tailored for both low and high load scenarios. Deep examination of the principles underlying seawater electrolysis for hydrogen production, including mathematical modeling of water migration and consumption. Experiments revealed the relationship between water migration rate and electrolyte solution concentration, and explored the variations in water migration rates across PTFE membranes with different pore sizes and areas. Physical experiments validated the accuracy and efficacy of the system modeling. Targeted recommendations for improvement were put forth, offering a reference for further refinement of seawater direct hydrogen production systems.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Phase-Shift Control Method to Suppress Current DC Bias for Bidirectional Dual-Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: This paper presents a method for suppressing transient dc bias of inductor current in dual-active bridge (DAB) converters, which is applicable to the frequently used modulation methods. The suggested method is applicable to widely adopted modulation techniques. Through the independent implementation of dynamic volt-seconds balancing for each half-bridge independently, the inductor current can swiftly attain the novel reference steady state while greatly suppressing transient dc-bias components. Concurrently, this method can eliminate the narrow pulse phenomenon. To validate the effectiveness of the suggested control strategy, simulations are performed.

articleTitle: A Full-ANN Control Method of Three-Phase Grid-Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: To break free from the confines of the d-q control framework and traditional control techniques, such as phase-locked loop, as well as proportional-integral/proportional-resonant controllers, this paper proposes a three-phase inverter grid-connected control method based on a full-artificial neural network (FANN-TPIGCC), which leverages the nonlinear approximation capabilities of artificial neural networks to directly obtain the modulation wave required for inverter control. First, the inverter circuit principle is analyzed and two sets of auxiliary variables are chosen. Subsequently, the first and second sets of auxiliary variables are separately input into two echo state networks based on the least square algorithm. These networks respectively output the reference modulation wave and the amplitude ratio along with the phase difference. Finally, utilizing the amplitude ratio and phase difference, a modulation transformation method is devised to fine-tune both amplitude and phase of the reference modulation wave, resulting in the ultimate modulation wave utilized for inverter grid-tied control. Simulink simulation results show that the FANN-TPIGCC method can achieve flexible switching between different reference current under both strong and weak grid conditions. It exhibits lower total harmonic distortion and ideal steady-state performance, meeting the control requirements of three-phase inverters.

articleTitle: Magnetic Integration Design of Multi-channel Parallel Flying Capacitor Boost Converter in Photovoltaic Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: For the high-voltage level photovoltaic energy storage system, the front-end DC/DC converter is often composed of multi-channel parallel flying capacitor Boost converter (FCBC). In order to further effectively reduce the size of the inductor and improve the power density of the converter, magnetic integration technology is introduced into multi-channel parallel FCBC. Due to the characteristics of photovoltaic modules, the coupled inductor needs to meet different operating conditions. The paper focuses on the working state of the FCBC under different operating conditions and derives the requirements for the coupled inductor parameters. Finally, a three-phase FCBC simulation circuit model is built in PLECS. The simulation results verify that the coupled inductor can accommodate diverse operating conditions, reduce current ripple and improve the steady-state performance of the converter effectively.

articleTitle: Thermal Regulation Fast Charging for Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries can shorten the electric vehicle's recharging time, effectively alleviating the range anxiety prevalent in electric vehicles. However, during fast charging, lithium plating occurs, resulting in loss of available lithium, especially under low-temperature environments and high charging rates. Increasing the battery temperature can mitigate lithium plating, but it will also aggravate other side reactions of aging, thereby contributing to the degradation of usable capacity and increasing potential safety hazards. This paper studies a commercial 18650 NCM lithium-ion battery and proposes a universal thermal regulation fast charging strategy that balances battery aging and charging time. An electrochemical coupling model considering temperature effects was built to determine the relationship between the allowable charging rate of the battery and both temperature and SOC (state of charge). Then the Pareto frontier is calculated using the NSGA-II algorithm, with the lithium plating boundary as the constraint and the battery aging and charging time as the optimization objectives. By weighing the battery aging and charging time, the temperature control strategy for the fastest charging speed when the battery meets the aging requirements is obtained.

articleTitle: TCM Control Without Zero-Crossing Detection for Buck Active Power Decoupler
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Buck active power decoupler (APD) can suppress DC side second harmonic current of single-phase converter. APD operating in triangular current mode (TCM) can realize zero-voltage switching (ZVS), improving efficiency and power density. However, traditional TCM control relies on modules such as zero-crossing detection and high-speed sampling, which require high-precision hardware and software. For easy implementation, a computation-based TCM control method is proposed in this paper, using low-frequency sampling of voltage and current signals. Furthermore, the stability of the voltage-current double closed-loop system is improved by introducing feedforward. Finally, the proposed control strategy is validated by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Multi-Timescale Operation and Planning for Electricity-Hydrogen Integrated Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: This paper investigates the planning and optimization of operations for an electricity-hydrogen-integrated energy system (EH-IES) to achieve the consumption of RESs and multiple load demand's supply. To deal with the mismatches between RESs and load demand in different timescales., a hybrid storage system including battery, heat and hydrogen storage is applied to EH-IES. Also, a multi-timescale operational strategy is proposed to coordinate these storage devices. Case studies in southeastern China's IES verify the effectiveness of our planning approach. Compared to the system with single battery storage, the usage of hydrogen storage could significantly increase economic benefits and the consumption of RESs. Moreover, the results reveal that the proposed multi-timescale operational strategy lowers equivalent annual costs by at least 21.3%.

articleTitle: Integrated Energy Optimization and Dispatch of a Park Microgrid with Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: This paper focuses on a park microgrid with electric vehicles, establishing a comprehensive economic cost dispatch model that includes both operational costs and environmental management costs. A Simulated Annealing-Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm is proposed to address this model. Through case study simulations, the integrated energy optimization and dispatch strategies of microgrids with electric vehicle clusters under different scenarios are analyzed. The results indicate that the participation of electric vehicle clusters in microgrid dispatch can significantly reduce economic costs, with strategies for the orderly charging of electric vehicles further optimizing the microgrid's scheduling efficiency. Compared to traditional particle swarm optimization, the SA-PSO algorithm demonstrates superior solution quality and convergence.

articleTitle: Modulation and Control for Soft-Switching Six-Switch Buck-Boost Converter with Reduced Inductor Current Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The bidirectional dc-dc converter plays a vital role for interfacing the energy storage units to the internal dc-bus in the power conditioning system. Compared to the commonly used four-switch buck-boost (FSBB) converter, the six-switch buck-boost (SSBB) converter offers the advantages of higher input voltage rating, wider input voltage range, and enhanced control flexibility. This paper investigates the modulation and control for the SSBB. The soft-switching modulation scheme is proposed for achieving zero-voltage-switching for all power switches, and the multiple mode control is proposed for minimizing the inductor current ripple throughout the entire input voltage and output load range. Finally, simulation results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: An Inductor-Voltage-Shaped Hysteresis Current Controller of the Parallel-Connected Bidirectional Buck/Boost Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The bidirectional buck/boost converters (BBBC) are widely used in electric vehicles to achieve bidirectional energy flow. To address high current demands, parallel-connected BBBC system are developed. The distributed control for the parallel BBBC system has the advantages of reliability and scalability. However, the interleaving lines are required to achieve the interleaving operation which decreases the reliability. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel hysteresis current controller for the two-module-paralleled BBBC to achieve the interleaving operation without the need for interleaving lines. The parallel structure with a common inductor is proposed first to provide the hardware basis. Then, the inductor-voltage-shaped hysteresis current controller is proposed to achieve the interleaving operation. The detailed analysis of the proposed controller is presented in this paper, and experiments are carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Parasitic Parameters Optimization of PCB Busbar for ANPC Converter using Hybrid Components
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Busbars integrate conductors, insulation, and terminals, facilitating the seamless connection of capacitors, power devices, and other components. A well-engineered busbar design minimizes parasitic elements, which is crucial for maintaining stable system performance. This article combines SiC MOSFET power modules, Si IGBT power modules, and discrete Si IGBT devices. By employing an optimization strategy, it refines the placement of components, the laminate sequencing, the positioning of terminals and capacitors to reduce the parasitic parameters of the current commutation loop (CCL), leading to an enhanced PCB laminated busbar design. To improve current-carrying capacity between the inner and outer PCB layers while minimizing inductance, via-in-pad technology is utilized. According to Q3D simulation, the parasitic inductance of the large CCLs are reduced to just 58.93 nH and 59.39 nH.

articleTitle: Design and Research of a Low Loss Start High Voltage Wide Range Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: With the rapid development of multi electric/all electric aircraft, active phased arrays, and fuel cells, the range of bus voltage is constantly increasing, and the power level is constantly increasing. At the same time, safety and conversion efficiency need to be considered. The number of isolation channels in the main conversion topology increases, and the parallel connection of multiple switching tubes brings greater power, wider input voltage range, and higher efficiency requirements to the auxiliary power source. To address this issue, research on the design of high-voltage wide range flyback converters is carried out. Firstly, the working mode and timing of the flyback converter are analyzed, and the expression of the output voltage gain of the converter under different modes is derived. Under extreme input conditions, a flyback transformer is designed based on the electromagnetic induction law and the Ampere loop law, where the transformer turn ratio is derived through the critical conduction mode; Secondly, small signal modeling is performed on the flyback converter and the transfer function is derived, followed by loop supplementary design based on the transfer function; Analyze the conventional RC startup circuit losses of the flyback converter and propose a low loss startup circuit that can switch to low loss mode after startup, further improving system efficiency; Finally, based on the analysis of the working principle and characteristics of the proposed converter, a 180-425V input, 5V output, 20<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> experimental prototype was designed, with an external size of 1/16 brick. The correctness of the theoretical analysis and the feasibility of the scheme were verified.

articleTitle: Circuit Design and Control of Independent-Input, Parallel-Output DC/DC Converters for Modular Battery Balancing
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The energy storage system consists of a large number of cells connected in series and parallel, and the inconsistency of the cells leads to a decrease in capacity utilization and system efficiency. In order to improve the granularity of system control, each modular battery is equipped with an isolated DC/DC converter, which adopts the architecture of parallel output between each module. In this paper, an isolated converter topology and its control method are proposed to realize the function of control the modular battery power flow. For the independent-input and parallel-output (IIPO) system, adaptive balancing control method is designed based on the balanced state of capacity (SOC) or current control objective, and verified by simulation. Finally, a 4.8kW prototype is built to verify the circuit design and control method.

articleTitle: Bidirectional AC-DC Converter Suitable for V2G System in Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: With the low-carbon transformation of energy and electricity, the new energy automobile industry has developed rapidly. Bidirectional interactive technology applied to Vehicle to Grid (V2G) has attracted much attention in virtual power plant. With V2G technology, it is possible to enhance the operational efficiency of the power grid and improve the capacity for resource allocation. However, because of the wide range of global grid voltage or lithium battery voltage, the existing bidirectional converter cannot always work in the best efficiency state. This paper proposed a bidirectional AC-DC converter uses the concept of flexible converter and incorporates the merits of single-phase full-bridge grid-connected inverter and T-type three-level inverter. The converter has the flexibility to select the most efficient operating mode depending on the input voltage, thus minimizing converter losses. The proposed converter is suitable for V2G system in virtual power plant

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a 400W DC/DC Module Achieving High Efficiency and High Power Density
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: With the increasing demand for all-in-one computers, gaming notebooks, ultra-thin OLED TVs and other devices, the demand for efficient and high power density hundred-watt power supplies is also increasing. In particular, all-in-one computers, ultra-thin OLED TVs and portable workstations have limited space left for power supplies, which presents huge challenge for related design. In this paper, a half bridge LLC resonant converter module is designed as the DC/DC power module. In order to improve efficiency, the resonant parameters of the half-bridge LLC are modeled and optimized in this paper, so that the RMS current is as small as possible and the primary side device realizes ZVS. In terms of device selection, through modeling and calculation, the scheme with the lowest loss is selected, and the high-integrated half-bridge GaN power IC is applied to further improve the power density. The final prototype uses the design of a planar transformer with integrated resonant inductors, and the high switching frequency of 500kHz further reduces the size of the magnetic element. The prototype is only 8mm thick and has a high power density of 21.5W/cm3 (62.5 x 37.2 x 8mm). Peak efficiency can be close to 98%, full load (400W) efficiency is 97.52%.

articleTitle: Design of an Improved Trans-Inductor Voltage Regulator
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: This article proposes an improved trans-inductor voltage regulator to mitigate output voltage overshoot and undershoot in voltage regulator modules during load step-change transients. In the improved TLVR, the energy stored in the trans-inductor for each phase is absorbed or released more quickly, enhancing the dynamic response of the TLVR. Simulation results indicate that, compared to the conventional TLVR, the improved TLVR reduces output voltage overshoot by 73%.

articleTitle: Design and Control of a Multi-Port Converter with Split Inductors
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: With the rapid development of new energy generation and distributed energy storage technologies, multi-port converters have increasingly become a hot research topic in the power electronics industry. Considering the duality between inductors and capacitors in circuit theory, this paper proposes a three-port three-level converter based on split inductors. Subsequently, the operational modes of the proposed topology are analyzed, and a feasible modulation strategy is proposed along with an analysis of the corresponding PWM signal generation logic. Finally, theoretical analysis and simulation results validate the correctness and feasibility of the proposed circuit topology and modulation strategy.

articleTitle: A Dual-Receiver Magnetic Coupler with Smooth Output for Dynamic Wireless Charging of Automated Guided Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: The technology known as dynamic wireless power transmission (DWPT) has great promise in reducing the weight and expense of automated guided vehicles (AGVs) by reducing the amount of battery capacity they carry. However, there are large mutual inductance and power fluctuation in the dynamic charging process. This paper suggests a low-cost, low-variation dual-receiver magnetic coupler that is coupled in parallel by two half-bridge rectifiers as a solution to this issue. An I-type solenoid coil is used to strengthen the coupling and magnetic field. The optimized design of the coupler structure enables the system to have smooth mutual inductance fluctuation. According to the simulated results, the equivalent mutual inductance fluctuation is 3.6%, confirming the viability of the magnetic coupling structure's optimized design and the efficacy of the suggested DWPT system.

articleTitle: Current-Source Flexible Transfer Converter for Autonomous Control of Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Flexible transfer converter (FTC) positioned at the grid interface can enable fully autonomous control of microgrids through automatic synchronization control (ASC), automatic frequency control (AFC) and automatic voltage control (AVC) and so on. Back-to-back (BTB) current source converter (CSC) shows potential advantages working as FTC, like smaller footprint and lower cost because of the elimination of step-up transformers. Different from the BTB voltage source converter, BTB CSC's dc voltage is not required to keep constant in operation. Considering this characteristic, the dc-link current minimization by modulation ratio maximization can be selected as the strategy to optimize the system efficiency. Its internal mechanism is analyzed in detail by comparing the quantitative relationship between degrees of freedom and controllable variables, indicating that the modulation ratio of CSC on one side should be maximized. On this basis, the control architecture of BTB CSC-based FTC is established, which includes the top layer control consisting of ASC, AFC and AVC as well as the bottom layer control for tracking power references. Finally, the effectiveness of current-source FTC with the proposed control strategy is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: A Unified Grid-Forming Structure with Power Control Capability for DFIG Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: In doubly-fed induction generator wind turbines (DFIG-WT), both the stator and grid-side converter can affect the voltage at its output terminal, making it more complicated to realize grid-forming control than Type-IV wind turbine and energy storage system. Current research on grid-forming DFIG-WT focuses on methods such as power synchronization control, VSG control without inner-loop, and dc-link voltage synchronization control. However, less consideration was given to reasonable cooperation between both sides to achieve better overall voltage source characteristics, and mode switching was inevitable to implement frequency dead zone and power limit control, which is commonly required in wind power generation. This paper analyzes the requirements of grid-forming control for DFIG-WT, and proposes a unified grid-forming control scheme that can achieve the aforementioned frequency dead zone and fast power control capability without mode switching, as well as providing desired inertia response and frequency regulation feature. Numerical simulation is carried out and validation result is presented.

articleTitle: Variable Seires Resistance of Output Capacitor Based on V2COT Control for Half-Bridge Current Doubler Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: 48V Voltage Regulator Modules (VRMs) are crucial to data center power supply. Control scheme of half-bridge current doubler rectifier (HBCDR) converter for VRM applications affects greatly on its transient responses. In this paper, a novel variable series resistance V2cotcontrol is proposed. Variation of ESR provides both optimal steady-state and transient responses. Characteristics of HBCDR converter is analyzed and proposed control scheme is applied to it, validating its performances. Finally, a prototype is built.

articleTitle: Recovery Overcurrent Analysis for Grid Forming Converter Under Symmetrical Fault with the Impact of Power Synchronization Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Due to the inherent self-synchronous voltage source characteristics of the grid forming (GFM) converter, its output current is significantly affected by power angle swing dynamics. Since the power angle swing is dominated by active power control, the transient current behavior during fault and recovery stage is closely related to the power synchronization dynamics, which needs detailed investigation. This paper proposed a transient current model of grid-connected GFM converter, which depicts the relationship between the current behavior and power angle motion. Moreover, the recovery overcurrent (ROC) boundary is quantitively characterized through the energy function to identify whether the ROC phenomenon occurs. On this basis, the impact of power synchronization dynamics on the ROC behavior is evaluated. It reveals that the reduction of active power control reference, the decrease of inertia constant, and the enhancement of damping coefficient in the active power control loop can help GFM converter avoid ROC phenomenon. The above analysis and discussion are well-validated in simulation platform.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Junction Temperature Estimation Method of Power Semiconductor Devices Based on Case Temperature Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: Junction temperature is the key factor affects the reliability of power semiconductor devices, and accurate junction temperature estimation is of great significance for converter reliability assessment. In this paper, the power device IGBT module is taken as a typical research object, a dynamic estimation method of junction temperature based on case temperature feedback is proposed. Firstly, the junction temperature loss calculation model and Cauer thermal network model of IGBT module are established, and the dynamic digital estimation algorithm of junction temperature is deduced; then, the loss characteristics and thermal response characteristics of the device are tested via the test platform; finally, the estimated junction temperature is experimentally validated using infrared temperature measurement, and the deviation of junction temperature is within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, which verifies the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis and Improvement for LCC-HVDC in Sending AC Grid with Wind Farms Based on Grid-Forming Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 CPSS & IEEE International Symposium on Energy Storage and Conversion (ISESC)
abstract: As the traditional power system undergoes a gradual transition towards a new-type power system with high incorporation of renewable energy sources, the dynamic interaction between these renewable energy sources, weak grid, and LCC-HVDC may potentially give rise to some concerns.
